## Maximum Entropy (MaxEnt)

This is based on Shannon's Entropy. In the diversity context it means the probability of finding a certain species in an area where we randomly select individuals, based on the relative abundances. The formula is given by

$H = -\sum_{i=1}^{S} p_i \ln(p_i)$

where S is the total number of species and p is the probability of finding the species i. A value of H=0 indicates a community containing only one species, whereas higher values indicate greater diversity. For a community with S species, the maximum value, H'_{\max} =ln(S), occurs when all species have equal relative abundance.

The MaxEnt algorithm is now finding the probability distribution with the heighest entropy under given constraints.

The example is done with the sloth data from the maxnet Package. A dataset containing environmental data at 116 Bradypus variegatus occurrence points and 1000 background points in South and Central America. 
See:
- Anderson, R. P. and Handley, Jr., C. O. (2001). A new species of three-toed sloth (Mammalia: Xenarthra) from Panama, with a review of the genus Bradypus. Proceedings of the Biological Society of Washington 114, 1-33.

- Phillips, S. J. et al. (2006). Maximum entropy modeling of species geographic distributions. Ecological Modelling 190, 231-259

# Data
Let's first take a look at the data. As you can see there is occurence data of the sloths, which is stored in the column "preseence" which can either be 1 or 0 for yes or no. There is additional background variables, which we use to determine the habitat structure and give to our model.

```{r Data, warning = FALSE, messages = FALSE}

data(bradypus, package = "maxnet")

# Datensatzstruktur untersuchen
str(bradypus)
head(bradypus)

names(bradypus)
summary(bradypus)


```
Here (all values between 1961 and 1990),
cld stands for annual cloud cover
dtr for annual day-night-temperature difference
ecoreg for categorial ecoregion
frst for annual occurence of frosting
h_dem for height
pre for the precipation for th months (11 for November)
tmn for the annual minimal temperature
tmp for the annual mean temperature
tmx for the annual max temperature
vap for the Water vapor pressure

In the next step we separate our data in a test and a training data set

```{r test and train data, wanrings = FALSE, messages = FALSE}
# create test dataset with 60 % of the data and train d<ta set with the rest
# creating an ID for the data so we can seperate them

set.seed(42)

brad <- bradypus %>%
  mutate(ID = row_number())

# 80% train and 20% test for present and absent each
train_brad <- brad %>%
  group_by(presence) %>%
  slice_sample(prop = 0.8) %>%
  ungroup()

test_brad <- brad %>%
  filter(!ID %in% train_brad$ID)

# show the distribution
table(train_brad$presence)
table(test_brad$presence)

```
Next we select the environmental parameters.
```{r env parameters}
# not our goal variable
p_train <- train_brad$presence
p_test  <- test_brad$presence

# env variables
x_train <- train_brad %>%
  select(-presence, -ID)

x_test <- test_brad %>%
  select(-presence, -ID)

#
str(x_train)
summary(x_train)

```
Now we train our MaxEnt model

```{r train model}
model <- maxnet(
  p = p_train,
  data = x_train,
  f = maxnet.formula(
    p_train,
    x_train,
    classes = "lqph"
  )
)

print(model)
```

```{r}
pred_test <- predict(
  model,
  newdata = x_test,
  type = "cloglog"
)

summary(pred_test)

```
```{r}
roc_model <- pROC::roc(
  response = p_test,
  predictor = as.numeric(pred_test),
  levels = c(0, 1),
  direction = "<",
  quiet = TRUE
)

plot(
  roc_model,
  main = "ROC curve – MaxEnt"
)

auc_value <- pROC::auc(roc_model)

print(auc_value)
```

```{r}
variable <- "tmp6190_ann"

# Prüfen, ob die Variable existiert
stopifnot(variable %in% names(x_train))

# Referenzdatensatz erstellen: Median für numerische Variablen,
# häufigste Kategorie für kategoriale Variablen
reference <- lapply(x_train, function(x) {
  if (is.numeric(x)) {
    median(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  } else {
    names(which.max(table(x)))
  }
})

reference <- as.data.frame(reference)

# Faktorstruktur von ecoreg beibehalten
for (nm in names(x_train)) {
  if (is.factor(x_train[[nm]])) {
    reference[[nm]] <- factor(
      reference[[nm]],
      levels = levels(x_train[[nm]])
    )
  }
}

# Temperaturgradient erzeugen
values <- seq(
  min(x_train[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
  max(x_train[[variable]], na.rm = TRUE),
  length.out = 100
)

# Referenzdatensatz 100-mal kopieren
newdata <- reference[rep(1, length(values)), , drop = FALSE]
rownames(newdata) <- NULL

# Nur die untersuchte Variable verändern
newdata[[variable]] <- values

# Vorhersagen berechnen
predictions <- predict(
  model,
  newdata = newdata,
  type = "cloglog"
)

# Ergebnisse visualisieren
response_data <- data.frame(
  temperature = values,
  prediction = as.numeric(predictions)
)

ggplot(response_data, aes(x = temperature, y = prediction)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Response Curve: mittlere Jahrestemperatur",
    x = "Mittlere Jahrestemperatur",
    y = "MaxEnt cloglog output"
  ) +
  theme_minimal()
```
